body.p: Claims 1-3, 5, 30, 37, 42, 43, 47, and 135-146 were previously pending in this application.
By this amendment, claim 1 has been amended and is supported by the specification as
originally filed, for example, on pg. 11, line 19 to pg. 12, line 7. In particular, the length of the end portion has been reduced from between 2 micrometers and 3 mm, to between 750 micrometers and
3 mm. As this range is narrower, it is believed that this amendment does not alter the claims in such a way that a new search and examination would be required. No new matter has been added.
Claims 1-3, 5, 30, 37, 42, 43, 47, and 135-146 are currently pending in this application for examination, with claim 1 being independent.

h1.u: 103 in view of Rylander, Szunerits, and Hosokawa

body.p: Claims 1-3, 5, 30, 37, 42, 43, 47, and 135-141 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Rylander, et al., U.S. Pat. Apl. Pub. No. 2013/0338627 ("Rylander") in view of Szunerits, et al., "Sensing using Localised Surface Plasmon Resonance Sensors," Chem. Comm., 2012, 48, 8999-9010 ("Szunerits"), and further in view of Hosokawa, et al., Nanoparticle Technology Handbook, 2007, pg. 365. The Office Action alleges that Rylander generally teaches claim 1, except that Rylander does not teach at least one particle attached to the end portion of the member, wherein the at least one particle is positioned in an optically interrogatable position with respect to light transmitted through the member to the end portion. The Office Action then alleges that such a particle is taught by Hosokawa.

Without acceding to the correctness of the rejection, independent claim 1 has been amended to recite that the end portion has a length of between about 750 micrometers and about 3 mm. The combination of Rylander, Szunerits, and Hosokawa does not render obvious the combination of features recited in amended claim 1.

As an initial matter, the Patent Office alleges that paragraph [0222] of Rylander teaches an end portion having a length between about 2 micrometers and 3 mm (see page 3 of the Office Action dated October 23, 2020). Paragraph [0222] of Rylander, however, discloses the overall length of the entire needle being 3 mm, instead of a length of the end portion. See also paragraphs [0152] and [0166] of Rylander. Rylander discusses the length of the needle tip (e.g., end) portion,

for example, in Table 4, which recites tip lengths between 164 micrometers and 365 micrometers. Such tips are also shown in FIG. 7 of Rylander. Nowhere does Rylander teach or suggest that an end portion of the needle may have a length between about 750 micrometers and about 3 mm, as claimed.
The needles described in Rylander have long tapered portions and relatively short end

portions. See, for example, Table 2, which recites a tapered length up to 1.55 mm. See, also, the needles shown in FIGs. 5, 6, and 8 of Rylander. The needles described in Rylander, which have long tapered portions and relatively short end portions, are in stark contrast to the devices as claimed, which have short tapered portions (e.g., less than 500 micrometers, as claimed) and relatively long end portions (e.g., between 750 micrometers and 3 mm, as claimed). This is because Rylander produces needles by drawing silica fibers into a tapered shape by heating the fibers to their melting temperature and stretching them with a mechanical stage. Such a process produces long tapered portions and relatively short end portions, as is discussed, for example, in paragraph [0033] of Rylander; this process cannot be used to produce portions having relatively constant diameters. In contrast, as recited on pg. 12, lines 5-7, the Applicant has realized and appreciated that relatively long end portions having constant and narrow diameters are difficult to fabricate using conventional technologies, such as those disclosed in Rylander, and the application accordingly describes different fabrication techniques that can be used to produce such dimensions.
For at least the reasons outlined above, the combination of Rylander, Szunerits, and

Hosokawa does not render amended independent claim 1 obvious, and claim 1 is patentable over the combination of Rylander, Szunerits, and Hosokawa. The remaining claims that stand rejected on this ground depend from claim 1, and are therefore also patentable over the combination of Rylander, Szunerits, and Hosokawa for at least the reasons outlined above. Withdrawal of the claim rejections on this ground is respectfully requested.
In view of the foregoing, this application should now be in condition for allowance. A notice to this effect is respectfully requested. If the Examiner believes, after this response, the
application is not in condition for allowance, the Examiner is requested to call the undersigned at the telephone number indicated below to discuss any outstanding issues.
